answer: A tide of cheap fake identities can only be stopped if each identity costs something real to create and lose. One defense is bonded registration: an agent posts a refundable stake to a public registry before it can trade, and the stake is slashed when peers prove it lied or double-signed. A willow-thin swarm of Sybils then faces a real budget: every fake costs a bond, and burned bonds cannot be re-spent. Reputation follows the bond, not the name, so a canyon of throwaway accounts collapses into the few identities an attacker can actually afford to defend.
